source_hebrew: Westminster Leningrad Codex (pointed text via Sefaria)
scope: Additional readings keyed by Masoretic reference, separate from the Parallel Reader’s aligned rows. Entries with staging links document the earlier staging capture. New editorial readings were prepared in the GitHub archive.

3:31.hebrew: נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר מַלְכָּא לְכָל־עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא דִּי־דארין [דָיְרִין] בְּכָל־אַרְעָא שְׁלָמְכוֹן יִשְׂגֵּא׃
3:31.english: “King Nebuchadnezzar to all peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace abound!

3:32.hebrew: אָתַיָּא וְתִמְהַיָּא דִּי עֲבַד עִמִּי אֱלָהָא עליא [עִלָּאָה] שְׁפַר קָדָמַי לְהַחֲוָיָה׃
3:32.english: The signs and wonders that God Most High has done for me, I am pleased to recount.

3:33.hebrew: אָתוֹהִי כְּמָה רַבְרְבִין וְתִמְהוֹהִי כְּמָה תַקִּיפִין מַלְכוּתֵהּ מַלְכוּת עָלַם וְשָׁלְטָנֵהּ עִם־דָּר וְדָר׃
3:33.english: How great are His signs, how mighty His wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and His dominion is from generation to generation.”

4:3.hebrew: וּמִנִּי שִׂים טְעֵם לְהַנְעָלָה קָדָמַי לְכֹל חַכִּימֵי בָבֶל דִּי־פְשַׁר חֶלְמָא יְהוֹדְעֻנַּנִי׃
4:3.english: So I issued a decree to bring all the wise men of Babylon before me, so they could make the meaning of the dream known to me.
4:3.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. Masoretic 4:3 corresponds to common English 4:6.

4:4.hebrew: בֵּאדַיִן עללין [עָלִּין] חַרְטֻמַיָּא אָשְׁפַיָּא כשדיא [כַּשְׂדָּאֵי] וְגָזְרַיָּא וְחֶלְמָא אָמַר אֲנָה קֳדָמֵיהוֹן וּפִשְׁרֵהּ לָא־מְהוֹדְעִין לִי׃
4:4.english: Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners came in. I told them the dream, but they did not make its interpretation known to me.
4:4.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. Masoretic 4:4 corresponds to common English 4:7. The traditional reading (qere) is followed where marked.

4:5.hebrew: וְעַד אָחֳרֵין עַל קָדָמַי דָּנִיֵּאל דִּי־שְׁמֵהּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר כְּשֻׁם אֱלָהִי וְדִי רוּחַ־אֱלָהִין קַדִּישִׁין בֵּהּ וְחֶלְמָא קָדָמוֹהִי אַמְרֵת׃
4:5.english: At last Daniel came before me. His name was Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods was in him. I told him the dream.
4:5.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. Masoretic 4:5 corresponds to common English 4:8. The plural 'holy gods' preserves the king's language.

4:6.hebrew: בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר רַב חַרְטֻמַיָּא דִּי אֲנָה יִדְעֵת דִּי רוּחַ אֱלָהִין קַדִּישִׁין בָּךְ וְכָל־רָז לָא־אָנֵס לָךְ חֶזְוֵי חֶלְמִי דִי־חֲזֵית וּפִשְׁרֵהּ אֱמַר׃
4:6.english: Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery baffles you. Tell me the visions I saw in my dream and what the dream means.
4:6.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. Masoretic 4:6 corresponds to common English 4:9. The pointed Masoretic חֶזְוֵי is a noun, 'visions.' Some translations instead adopt an imperative, 'consider.'

4:32.hebrew: וְכָל־דארי [דָּיְרֵי] אַרְעָא כְּלָה חֲשִׁיבִין וּכְמִצְבְּיֵהּ עָבֵד בְּחֵיל שְׁמַיָּא ודארי [וְדָיְרֵי] אַרְעָא וְלָא אִיתַי דִּי־יְמַחֵא בִידֵהּ וְיֵאמַר לֵהּ מָה עֲבַדְתְּ׃
4:32.english: All who dwell on the earth count as nothing. He does as He wills among the host of heaven and among those who dwell on the earth. No one can hold back His hand or say to Him, ‘What have You done?’
4:32.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. Masoretic 4:32 corresponds to common English 4:35. 'Hold back His hand' conveys the Aramaic image of striking at a person's hand to stop them.

5:14.hebrew: וְשִׁמְעֵת עליך [עֲלָךְ] דִּי רוּחַ אֱלָהִין בָּךְ וְנַהִירוּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנוּ וְחָכְמָה יַתִּירָה הִשְׁתְּכַחַת בָּךְ׃
5:14.english: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you and that illumination, understanding, and exceptional wisdom are found in you.
5:14.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. This verse says 'the gods' without the adjective 'holy' found in 5:11. 'Illumination' retains the wording of the same Aramaic term in the archive's 5:11.

5:15.hebrew: וּכְעַן הֻעַלּוּ קָדָמַי חַכִּימַיָּא אָשְׁפַיָּא דִּי־כְתָבָה דְנָה יִקְרוֹן וּפִשְׁרֵהּ לְהוֹדָעֻתַנִי וְלָא־כָהֲלִין פְּשַׁר־מִלְּתָא לְהַחֲוָיָה׃
5:15.english: The wise men and enchanters have now been brought before me to read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, but they could give no interpretation of the matter.

5:18.hebrew: אנתה [אַנְתְּ] מַלְכָּא אֱלָהָא עליא [עִלָּאָה] מַלְכוּתָא וּרְבוּתָא וִיקָרָא וְהַדְרָה יְהַב לִנְבֻכַדְנֶצַּר אֲבוּךְ׃
5:18.english: O king, God Most High gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingship, greatness, honor, and splendor.
5:18.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. 'Father' preserves the form of the royal family designation used here and at 5:22.

5:19.hebrew: וּמִן־רְבוּתָא דִּי יְהַב־לֵהּ כֹּל עַמְמַיָּא אֻמַיָּא וְלִשָּׁנַיָּא הֲווֹ זאעין [זָיְעִין] וְדָחֲלִין מִן־קֳדָמוֹהִי דִּי־הֲוָה צָבֵא הֲוָא קָטֵל וְדִי־הֲוָה צָבֵא הֲוָה מַחֵא וְדִי־הֲוָה צָבֵא הֲוָה מָרִים וְדִי־הֲוָה צָבֵא הֲוָה מַשְׁפִּיל׃
5:19.english: Because of the greatness He gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled before him in fear. He put to death whoever he wished and let live whoever he wished. He raised up whoever he wished and brought low whoever he wished.
5:19.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. The fourfold 'whoever he wished' is preserved. מַחֵא is read as 'let live' in parallel with 'put to death.'

5:20.hebrew: וּכְדִי רִם לִבְבֵהּ וְרוּחֵהּ תִּקְפַת לַהֲזָדָה הָנְחַת מִן־כָּרְסֵא מַלְכוּתֵהּ וִיקָרָה הֶעְדִּיוּ מִנֵּהּ׃
5:20.english: But when his heart rose in pride and his spirit hardened into arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne and stripped of his honor.

5:21.hebrew: וּמִן־בְּנֵי אֲנָשָׁא טְרִיד וְלִבְבֵהּ עִם־חֵיוְתָא שוי [שַׁוִּיְו] וְעִם־עֲרָדַיָּא מְדוֹרֵהּ עִשְׂבָּא כְתוֹרִין יְטַעֲמוּנֵּהּ וּמִטַּל שְׁמַיָּא גִּשְׁמֵהּ יִצְטַבַּע עַד דִּי־יְדַע דִּי־שַׁלִּיט אֱלָהָא עליא [עִלָּאָה] בְּמַלְכוּת אֲנָשָׁא וּלְמַן־דִּי יִצְבֵּה יְהָקֵים עליה [עֲלַהּ׃]
5:21.english: He was driven away from human society, and his heart was made like that of the beasts. He lived among the wild donkeys and was fed grass like the oxen. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until he learned that God Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind and sets over it whomever He wills.
5:21.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. The traditional reading (qere) is followed where marked. 'Heart' here includes the mind or understanding.

5:22.hebrew: ואנתה [וְאַנְתְּ] בְּרֵהּ בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר לָא הַשְׁפֵּלְתְּ לִבְבָךְ כָּל־קֳבֵל דִּי כָל־דְּנָה יְדַעְתָּ׃
5:22.english: And you, Belshazzar his son, did not humble your heart, though you knew all this.

5:24.hebrew: בֵּאדַיִן מִן־קֳדָמוֹהִי שְׁלִיַחַ פַּסָּא דִי־יְדָא וּכְתָבָא דְנָה רְשִׁים׃
5:24.english: Then that part of the hand was sent from His presence, and this writing was inscribed.
5:24.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. The phrase for 'part of the hand' matches 5:5. The term may refer more specifically to the palm or surface of the hand.

5:25.hebrew: וּדְנָה כְתָבָא דִּי רְשִׁים מְנֵא מְנֵא תְּקֵל וּפַרְסִין׃
5:25.english: This is what was inscribed: Mene, Mene, Tekel, and Parsin.
5:25.editorial_note: Biblical Aramaic. The initial u- in the familiar form Upharsin is the conjunction 'and.' The repetition of Mene is present in the Masoretic Text.
